items.title: Malaysia and Singapore step up Nvidia AI chip probes amidst Jensen Huang controversy
items.description: Malaysia is investigating possible re-exports of Nvidia AI hardware amid concerns about circumvention of U.S. restrictions on China as Singapore charges an executive over suspicious purchases of 917 AI servers.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Malaysia and Singapore have intensified scrutiny of AI hardware shipments amid concerns about the potential circumvention of U.S. export restrictions on China. Malaysia has launched an investigation into whether AI hardware imported by a subsidiary of the ill-fated Megaspeed was subsequently exported to other countries, reports Reuters. Meanwhile, Singapore has charged another executive over questionable purchases of 917 servers that may contain Nvidia accelerators, according to The Straits Times. The news follows the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over claims he had multiple extra-marital affairs, including with a possible Chinese intelligence asset who facilitated GPU smuggling into China. Analysts speculate that systematic chip smuggling may be the reason behind his departure.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedMalaysia's Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry is examining whether Speedmatrix, the Malaysian subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed, re-exported any of the AI processors and servers it had imported for use in local data centers. Apparently, after months of investigating, authorities have yet to find out whether any such shipments occurred and, if they did, whether they complied with Malaysian laws. Malaysia introduced restrictions on the export, transit, and trans-shipment of advanced U.S.-developed AI accelerators in July 2025, so it now requires companies to obtain appropriate permits.The Malaysian ministry said it was cooperating with customs authorities as well as officials in Singapore and the U.S., and could introduce additional restrictions. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said there was no evidence that Megaspeed-related AI hardware had left Malaysia, but he promised to cooperate with international investigations.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Speaking of Megaspeed, the company said on November 12 that it had hired a U.S. law firm to conduct a comprehensive inventory of its AI GPUs and independently assess its compliance with U.S. export-control regulations, reports DigiTimes. The company also confirmed that it had cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and was prepared to cooperate with other U.S. government agencies if necessary.James Tan Yong Pong, chief executive of Megaspeed, stressed that compliance with U.S. export rules as well as transparent operations were always a priority for the company. However, Megaspeed did not disclose how many GPUs it owns and which GPU models it has, what BIS examined during its inspections, or whether the authorities had identified any violations. You may like Nvidia tightens tracking of AI GPUs in Southeast Asia as Chinese chip smuggling draws scrutiny, report claims Mass smuggling of up to 1.5 million Nvidia AI GPUs could be the underlying cause of Jensen Huang's departure, analysts claim Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims Meanwhile, Singaporean authorities have brought 41 criminal charges against Shi Bingzhe, a 34-year-old Chinese citizen who served as director of Superphi and chief operating officer of NJ Global Financial. The two companies purchased 917 servers containing restricted Nvidia hardware from Aperia International in 41 transactions between May 2024 and February 2025, according to prosecutors. Authorities allege that the companies had reason to believe the servers were linked to criminal activity by Aperia International. Superphi now faces six charges, while NJ Global Financial faces 35.The latest charges expand a case that now involves five individuals and six companies. Four firms — Aperia International, A-Speed Infotech, Aperia Cloud Services (II), and Luxuriate Your Life — were charged in July over allegedly making false claims when purchasing servers. Meanwhile, the exact nature of those claims was not disclosed in the report. Authorities have frozen the disposal of a property worth approximately S$55 million and confiscated around S$1 million from bank accounts. Shi faces up to 10 years in prison and a fine of S$500,000 per charge if convicted. His next court appearance is scheduled for January 4, 2027.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe two cases largely highlight the significance of Malaysia and Singapore in the supply chain of restricted AI hardware to places where it should not be, such as China. Singapore's investigation focuses on alleged fraud and transactions involving proceeds of criminal activity, whereas Malaysia seeks to find out whether imported AI equipment was subsequently shipped abroad in violation of local regulations.Neither investigation has found that the hardware ultimately reached China, but both illustrate difficulties that authorities face as they attempt to enforce restrictions on advanced AI hardware across international supply chains. items.titleZh: 马来西亚和新加坡在黄仁勋争议中加强对英伟达AI芯片的调查
items.descriptionZh:
这篇报道聚焦美国对华先进AI芯片出口限制背景下，马来西亚和新加坡对AI硬件转运与走私风险的执法升级。文章称，马来西亚正在调查已陷入风波的Megaspeed旗下马来西亚子公司Speedmatrix，是否将原本进口用于本地数据中心的AI处理器和服务器再出口至其他国家；新加坡则就917台可能含有Nvidia加速器的服务器采购问题，对另一名高管提出刑事指控。原文还将这些调查与所谓Nvidia CEO黄仁勋因婚外情及可能涉及中国情报资产而辞职的传闻联系起来，并称分析师猜测系统性芯片走私可能是其离职原因。需要指出，这部分说法缺乏公开证据支持，摘要仅反映原文叙述。

背景上，美国限制先进AI加速器对华出口，东南亚被视为可能的转口和转运节点。马来西亚投资、贸易和工业部正在核查Speedmatrix是否违反当地规定。马来西亚于2025年7月对美国开发的高级AI加速器的出口、过境和转运实施限制，要求相关企业取得许可。马方表示正与海关、新加坡和美国官员合作，并可能出台更多限制。马来西亚总理安瓦尔·易卜拉欣称，没有证据显示与Megaspeed相关的AI硬件已离开马来西亚，但承诺配合国际调查。

Megaspeed于11月12日称已聘请美国律所对其AI GPU进行全面盘点，并独立评估其是否符合美国出口管制规定；公司还确认配合美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）检查，并准备在必要时配合其他美国政府机构。CEO James Tan Yong Pong强调，遵守美国出口规则和透明运营始终是公司优先事项。但Megaspeed未披露其GPU数量、型号、BIS检查具体内容，也未说明当局是否发现违规。

新加坡方面，34岁中国公民Shi Bingzhe被控41项刑事罪名。他曾任Superphi董事和NJ Global Financial首席运营官。检方称，两家公司在2024年5月至2025年2月间通过41笔交易，从Aperia International购买917台含受限Nvidia硬件的服务器，并有理由相信这些服务器与Aperia International的犯罪活动有关。Superphi面临6项指控，NJ Global Financial面临35项。案件已涉及5名个人和6家公司；Aperia International、A-Speed Infotech、Aperia Cloud Services (II)和Luxuriate Your Life四家公司此前因购买服务器时涉嫌虚假陈述于7月被控，但报道未披露虚假陈述的具体性质。当局冻结了价值约5500万新元财产的处置，并从银行账户没收约100万新元。若罪名成立，Shi每项罪名最高可判10年监禁及50万新元罚款，下次出庭定于2027年1月4日。

从技术原理看，此类案件的核心不是新产品创新，而是先进AI加速器出口管制与供应链合规。受限GPU通常用于数据中心的大规模AI训练和推理，具有高算力、高带宽和高价值特征，是美国对华技术限制的重点。规避路径可能包括第三国转口、过境转运、虚假最终用户声明、整机与部件混装、以及利用区域数据中心作为名义最终用途等。马来西亚的新许可制度正是针对出口、过境和转运环节补上监管缺口；新加坡案件则侧重欺诈、虚假陈述和犯罪所得交易。

原文未提供具体GPU型号、算力、带宽、功耗等性能参数，也没有不同芯片之间的性能对比数据。可量化的信息主要是：917台服务器、41笔交易、41项指控、5名个人和6家公司、约5500万新元冻结财产、约100万新元没收金额、每项罪名最高10年监禁和50万新元罚款，以及马来西亚2025年7月的管制措施和Megaspeed 11月12日的合规声明。

影响和应用场景方面，两起案件说明新加坡和马来西亚在受限AI硬件供应链中的关键节点地位，也显示各国执法机构在跨国供应链中追踪最终流向的难度。对数据中心运营商、服务器集成商和云服务商而言，需要加强最终用户审查、转售和再出口合规、GPU资产盘点与可追溯性。两起调查均尚未认定相关硬件最终进入中国，但已凸显美国出口限制在东南亚执行中的复杂性和合规风险。

items.titleZh: 黄仁勋传奇中真正利害攸关的是什么
items.descriptionZh:
本期The Vergecast以英伟达CEO黄仁勋从这家“AI最重要公司”的最高职位辞职为切入点，讨论这可能只是更大故事的开端：英伟达在中国市场的交易、美国政府为保护强大盟友而可能选择性忽视相关问题，以及整个AI行业的稳定性。节目称，接下来公众将了解更多关于Megaspeed的信息，并听到更多人——尤其是新当选的民主党人——追问“谁知道什么、何时知道”。同时，节目还提出谁将接替黄仁勋成为AI行业的“前台人物”，以及相关各方能否经受即将到来的审查。

随后，节目汇总了流媒体服务领域一系列看似不大的新闻，认为它们共同构成好莱坞应对TikTok的计划：微剧、免费层以及对垂直视频的深度投入，能否拯救Netflix、Paramount等公司。节目判断效果可能不佳，但这是唯一理性的尝试。最后在闪电轮中，讨论了“Brendan Carr Is a Dummy”、马克·扎克伯格的AI实验、Cybertruck时代等话题。节目还提到私密种子追踪器、Apple HomeView评测、听众热线提问以及对黄仁勋事件的多次讨论，并呼吁听众通过热线、邮件联系和订阅节目。

需要说明的是，原文是播客节目介绍/讨论提纲，并未展开核心技术原理、创新点、性能参数或对比数据；其技术影响主要体现在英伟达在华业务与AI产业稳定性、流媒体平台应对短视频竞争，以及AI实验等应用和产业议题上。

items.title: ‘Broken and shattered’ Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang surrendered during resignation meeting, report claims
items.description: Jensen Huang reportedly called himself 'a piece of sh--" after his forced departure, but employees still want him back.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 39 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly called himself “a piece of sh**" as he left the company he built over 33 years. Bloomberg reports that the co-founder, known for his legendary energy and outgoing demeanor, surrendered and looked “broken and shattered” during the board meeting where he resigned from the AI hardware firm after admitting to at least one extra-marital affair, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. But despite his resignation and the controversies surrounding him, it seems that Nvidia employees are still rallying behind him, with thousands of comments on the company’s internal “suggestion box” showing support for the disgraced leader, according to Wired.“If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” one commenter said, while another one wrote, “We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance.” An Nvidia staffer told Wired privately, “Nvidia is Nvidia because of Jensen,” even as another employee sent a company-wide email demanding transparency into his resignation. “I stand by Jensen. Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us.” They also added, “If America fails the man who helped build its future, then this world does not deserve Jensen Huang.”According to the report, internal calls for Huang's reinstatement have drawn more than 1,600 comments on Nvidia's internal forums, "the majority in full support of reinstalling him." The company has more than 42,000 employees worldwide.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Rumors about Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, being close to Jensen Huang first circulated in late October, with Nvidia vehemently denying there was any impropriety. “Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” an Nvidia spokesperson told Tom's Hardware. However, things took a turn for the worse for the Nvidia CEO when reports came out that he actually had an affair with Ms. Huang.Nvidia General Counsel and Secretary of the Board Tim Teter confronted Jensen at his house when this came out, after which he confessed. The founder soon released a statement admitting to and apologizing for his actions, while the company’s board formed an independent committee to investigate. However, another scandal broke out revealing that the former Nvidia chief had another affair — this time with a subordinate. This was apparently the last straw for the board, and the Nvidia co-founder was forced to resign soon after. You may like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits to having an affair with suspected Chinese spy Nvidia’s Board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang as second extra-marital affair emerges Elon Musk says it ‘would be an honor’ to hire ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Reports say that Jensen Huang was a hands-on leader, with over 60 executives at the company reporting directly to him, and that he was known to respond to emails quickly, whether it was day or night. But, more importantly, he was the face of the company who was particularly loved by many people, giving rise to the term “Jensanity” in his home country of Taiwan. Regardless of his status as a billionaire, people still find him trying out street food, eating at fast food chains, and even honoring his humble beginnings as a busboy at Denny’s.Aside from these latest scandals, many gamers castigate Huang for abandoning the core market that supported Nvidia before it became an AI giant, with consumer graphics cards now drastically more expensive than ever before. He was also often criticized for his all-out push on artificial intelligence and stance on selling chips to China. Still, those issues did not detract from his aura, with his trademark leather jacket raising nearly $1 million at a charity auction. It remains to be seen what will happen to Jensen after his monumental fall from grace, with SpaceX and Tesla mogul Elon Musk noting it would be an honor to hire Huang.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Download the Tom's Hardware app for up-to-the-minute updates on iOS and Android. items.titleZh: ‘Broken and shattered’ Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang surrendered during resignation meeting, report claims
items.descriptionZh:
这篇英文报道以“前英伟达CEO黄仁勋辞职”为叙事核心，称其在执掌英伟达33年后离开公司，并在董事会会议上承认至少一段婚外情，其中包括与疑似中国间谍、Megaspeed高管Alice Huang的关系。文章称，黄仁勋在辞职时情绪崩溃，甚至自称“a piece of sh**”；但英伟达内部论坛出现大量支持声音，约1600多条评论中多数要求其复职，员工称“英伟达之所以是英伟达，是因为黄仁勋”，并有人认为应给人第二次机会。报道还称，10月底有关Alice Huang与黄仁勋关系密切的传闻已出现，英伟达当时坚决否认存在不当行为，强调CEO与客户会面属正常工作；但后续报道称黄仁勋确实与Alice Huang有婚外情，公司总法律顾问Tim Teter在其家中对质后，黄仁勋承认并道歉，董事会成立独立委员会调查；随后又曝出他与一名下属存在第二段婚外情，董事会最终要求其辞职。

文章回顾了黄仁勋的管理风格和个人形象：他是亲力亲为的领导者，曾有60多名高管直接向他汇报，且无论昼夜都快速回复邮件；他在台湾因高人气被称为“Jensanity”，尽管是亿万富翁，仍被看到吃街头小吃、快餐，并提及自己早年曾在Denny’s当服务员。文章也提到他近年受到的批评，包括英伟达消费级显卡价格大幅上涨、被认为背离支持公司早期发展的游戏市场，以及全力押注人工智能和在对华芯片销售上的立场。其标志性皮夹克曾在慈善拍卖中筹得近100万美元；马斯克则表示，若雇佣黄仁勋将是一种荣幸。

需要指出的是，原文主要围绕人事丑闻、公司内部反应和个人形象展开，并未涉及任何AI芯片架构、技术原理、性能参数、竞品对比或具体应用场景，因此无法从该文中提炼芯片技术层面的创新点与性能分析。更重要的是，这篇报道的叙述与公开事实明显不符——黄仁勋仍是英伟达CEO——相关内容应视为未经证实、真实性存疑的传闻或虚构叙事，而非可靠的产业新闻。

items.titleZh: 我们来聊聊黄仁勋的诸多风流韵事！
items.descriptionZh:
这篇英文文章并非严格意义上的芯片技术报道，而是一篇带有强烈讽刺和八卦口吻的科技媒体评论/直播预告。文章围绕英伟达CEO黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）近期被戏谑讨论的个人绯闻展开，称其“新绯闻对象”不断出现，甚至调侃正在接近“绯闻奇点”，并讽刺地提出“AI的未来是否真的取决于黄仁勋的私生活”。随后文章把话题转向其认为真正重要的问题：“芯片与中国”。

文章称，美国总统特朗普据报在去年以及今年5月访华前，曾被警告Alice Huang可能与中国间谍机构存在关联；同时，英伟达据报介入了美国商务部对Alice Huang所涉公司的一项调查。原文以“Alice是否‘靠近太阳’过头”等讽刺性表述质疑相关事件，并引申到对CEO职责、AI作为生产力工具是否真能“解放所有人去同时经营多段绯闻”等调侃。文章最后是直播预告：作者与Nilay将于美东时间下午1点与读者讨论上述话题。

需要说明的是，原文没有提供芯片架构、技术原理、创新点、性能参数或应用场景等技术细节，也没有给出可验证证据，更多是评论、八卦化叙述和直播预热。因此无法从该文提炼AI芯片技术分析；其核心信息是围绕英伟达领导层个人绯闻、与中国相关的安全审查传闻、美国商务部调查及英伟达据称介入调查等展开的地缘政治与公司治理话题。

items.title: Mass smuggling of up to 1.5 million Nvidia AI GPUs could be the underlying cause of Jensen Huang's departure, analysts claim
items.description: Top analyst firm SemiAnalysis says it has tracked staggering 1.5 gigawatts of banned AI accelerators flowing into China.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 11 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Leading semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis believes that Jensen Huang's sudden departure from Nvidia may have been driven not only by revelations about his personal extramarital relationships, but also by widespread illicit exports of advanced AI accelerators to China. In its latest newsletter, analysts estimate that more than 1.5 gigawatts (GW) worth of restricted Nvidia hardware, which could be equivalent to up to 1.5 million GPUs, has reached the country despite U.S. export controls.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedOver 1.5 GW of Nvidia hardware subject to U.S. export restrictions ultimately ended up in China in recent years, according to SemiAnalysis' Accelerator Model, which tracks AI accelerator production and destinations. The estimate excludes processors that Nvidia specifically developed to comply with U.S. export rules, such as the H20 or H800. The firm also claims that the U.S. Department of Commerce has reached a similar conclusion about the scale of unauthorized shipments. Yet, SemiAnalysis does not disclose the exact number of accelerators shipped to China illegally, or their split between Nvidia's product generations.The scale of the alleged diversions is particularly notable because modern AI accelerators require substantial power and infrastructure. While the report does not explain how it converts accelerator quantities into power figures, it is likely that the company uses package-level nameplate/rated power multiplied by the number of GPUs. Assuming that all of these AI GPUs were Nvidia H200 SXM rated for up to 700W, then China got around 2.142 million of such accelerators, while if all of these processors were B200 SXM rated for up to 1,000W, then we are talking about 1.5 million units. For a mixed deployment, the total would fall between these figures, depending on the proportion of H200 and B200 accelerators. To put these numbers into context, xAI's Colossus One had 220-230,000 Hopper H100 and H200 GPUs, whereas the Colossus 2 has a target of 1.2 million Blackwell B200 and B300 GPUs. That said, 1.5 GW of restricted Nvidia hardware in China represents an enormous amount of computing infrastructure, which is comparable, or even exceeds, the scale of xAI's entire existing Colossus operation.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While SemiAnalysis did not reveal all the cases in which restricted AI accelerators reached the People's Republic of China, it supports its assessment with two well-known cases of alleged GPU smuggling. The first involves Supermicro co-founder Wally Liaw, Taiwan sales executive Steven Chang, and contractor Willy Sun, who were charged in March 2026. According to the indictment, approximately $2.5 billion worth of servers were sold to a company in Southeast Asia, with $510 million worth of equipment subsequently diverted to China and obtained by Alibaba. Prosecutors allege that the defendants used substitute servers and transferred identification labels to conceal the actual destinations of the hardware during audits.The second case involves nine individuals associated with Nvidia, Albatron, Chief Telecom, Flying Tiger, and Supermicro in Taiwan. The authorities accuse the group of arranging unauthorized exports of 130 Nvidia B300-based servers, 74 of which eventually reached China. The suspects used shell companies, forged documents, and declared Japan as the destination for servers that were actually bound for China, according to prosecutors. Taiwanese authorities discovered the operation during a drug smuggling investigation. Both cases are still before the courts. You may like How Shanghai fund manager Kang Wei introduced his wife Alice Huang to Jensen and built $7.5 billion Nvidia AI GPU smuggling operation Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims Amidst the ongoing fallout and reports into Jensen's Huang's extramarital affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence asset who was an executive at Megaspeed, one report claims that Ms. Huang was personally responsible for facilitating the smuggling of $7.5 billion of Nvidia AI hardware into China, around 240,000 GPUs, mostly H100 and H200 models.The right timing?SemiAnalysis suggests that the scale of these violations may explain why Huang's personal conduct became a major issue at this very point in time. The company's analysts speculate that some members of the U.S. intelligence community sought to remove Jensen Huang because he opposed more aggressive restrictions on China's access to American AI hardware. However, the report provides no direct evidence that intelligence agencies influenced Nvidia's board or that Huang participated in unauthorized exports.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe timing also coincides with congressional efforts to advance the Remote Access Security Act (RASA), which passed the House of Representatives on January 12. The legislation is meant to extend U.S. export-control authority to remote access to advanced AI hardware hosted outside China, including data centers in Europe and the Middle East. SemiAnalysis reports that Nvidia and Oracle have actively opposed the proposal.The analysts believe that Huang's departure essentially removes an influential opponent of stricter restrictions and accelerates efforts to block Chinese companies from accessing American AI hardware in the cloud. However, SemiAnalysis warns that truly all-inclusive restrictions could encourage Chinese developers to adopt domestic accelerators (something that Jensen Huang has consistently warned about), undermine international AI software collaboration, and ultimately weaken American high-tech companies.Continued Chinese access to American AI accelerators offers several advantages to the U.S. technology industry, according to SemiAnalysis. Firstly, it generates revenue for American companies such as AMD, Nvidia, and cloud service providers. Secondly, when Chinese companies rent GPU capacity from data centers outside China, U.S. authorities retain the ability to monitor their activities and potentially terminate access if necessary due to national security concerns. Thirdly, prolonged reliance on American hardware reduces incentives for Chinese developers to adopt domestic AI accelerators, which could eventually compete with AMD and Nvidia in international markets. What to read next Nvidia tightens tracking of AI GPUs in Southeast Asia as Chinese chip smuggling draws scrutiny, report claims Chinese AI companies buy 1 million Nvidia GPUs in a single year, report claims Alice Huang reportedly instrumental in securing over $7.5 billion of Nvidia AI GPU imports during three-year relationship with Jensen Huang Another important aspect is the contribution of Chinese developers to the global software ecosystem. On the one hand, Chinese laboratories have developed open-source technologies such as DeepEP, DeepGEMM, and MSA, which improve the efficiency of AI workloads on Nvidia hardware and benefit developers worldwide. In addition, American companies also depend on Chinese engineers, component suppliers, and manufacturers. Therefore, legal curbs that completely restrict Chinese developers' access to American AI accelerators could undermine international cooperation, reduce availability of open-source optimizations, and encourage Chinese companies to develop software specifically for domestic hardware.On the other hand, access to advanced AI accelerators from AMD or Nvidia enables Chinese laboratories to develop increasingly sophisticated AI models, which will rival leading-edge models developed in America and perhaps create national security risks. To that end, SemiAnalysis acknowledges the need to limit China's access to advanced AI accelerators from U.S.-based companies, as they could, among other things, be used to develop weapons of mass destruction or undermine American national security in different ways. Yet, SA analysts argue that restrictions should focus on the amount and capabilities of hardware available to Chinese entities rather than completely prohibit any access.SemiAnalysis seems to favor a system in which Chinese developers can rent computing capacity from trusted providers outside China under U.S. oversight. Such an approach could preserve American technological influence and commercial benefits and limit China's ability to acquire advanced AI infrastructure independently. items.titleZh: 分析师称，多达150万块英伟达AI GPU的大规模走私可能是黄仁勋离职的根本原因
items.descriptionZh:
据半导体研究机构SemiAnalysis分析，英伟达CEO黄仁勋突然离开英伟达，可能不仅与其个人婚外情曝光有关，也与大量受美国出口管制的先进AI加速器流入中国有关。SemiAnalysis在其最新通讯中估计，近年来已有超过1.5吉瓦（GW）的受限英伟达硬件进入中国，按不同GPU型号折算，相当于最多约150万块GPU。该估算来自其“Accelerator Model”，该模型追踪AI加速器的生产和最终目的地，并排除了英伟达为符合美国出口规则而专门开发的产品，如H20和H800。SemiAnalysis还称，美国商务部对未授权出货规模得出了类似结论，但未披露非法输华加速器的确切数量及代际分布。

1.5GW这一规模之所以引人关注，是因为现代AI加速器需要大量电力和基础设施。报告未说明如何将加速器数量换算为功率，但很可能是用封装级额定功率乘以GPU数量。若全部按最高700W的英伟达H200 SXM计算，中国获得约214.2万块此类加速器；若全部按最高1000W的B200 SXM计算，则约为150万块；混合部署则介于两者之间。作为对比，xAI的Colossus One拥有22万至23万块Hopper H100和H200 GPU，Colossus 2的目标是120万块Blackwell B200和B300 GPU。也就是说，1.5GW受限英伟达硬件所代表的算力基础设施规模巨大，可与xAI现有整个Colossus运营规模相当，甚至更大。

SemiAnalysis并未披露受限AI加速器进入中国的所有案例，但用两个已知的GPU走私案支撑其判断。第一案涉及Supermicro联合创始人Wally Liaw、台湾销售主管Steven Chang和承包商Willy Sun，三人于2026年3月被起诉。起诉书称，约25亿美元的服务器被卖给东南亚一家公司，其中5.1亿美元设备随后被转往中国并由阿里巴巴获得；被告据称在审计期间使用替代服务器和转移识别标签来掩盖硬件的真实目的地。第二案涉及与英伟达、Albatron、Chief Telecom、Flying Tiger和Supermicro台湾相关的九名个人。当局指控该团伙安排130台基于英伟达B300的服务器未经授权出口，其中74台最终到达中国。检方称，嫌疑人使用空壳公司、伪造文件，并将实际运往中国的服务器申报为日本目的地；台湾当局是在一项毒品走私调查中发现该操作的。两案目前仍在法院审理中。

另有报道称，在与黄仁勋保持三年关系的Alice Huang期间，她据称促成约75亿美元的英伟达AI硬件、约24万块GPU（多为H100和H200）进入中国。SemiAnalysis暗示，这些违规行为的规模可能解释为何黄仁勋的个人行为在此时成为重大问题。其分析师猜测，美国情报界部分成员可能希望移除黄仁勋，因为他反对更激进地限制中国获取美国AI硬件。但报告没有提供直接证据表明情报机构影响了英伟达董事会，或黄仁勋参与了未授权出口。

这一时间点也恰逢美国国会推进《远程访问安全法案》（RASA）。该法案于1月12日在众议院通过，旨在将美国出口管制权限扩展到对中国境外先进AI硬件的远程访问，包括欧洲和中东的数据中心。SemiAnalysis称，英伟达和甲骨文积极反对该提案。分析人士认为，黄仁勋的离开实质上移除了更严格限制的一位有影响力反对者，并可能加速阻止中国公司通过云端访问美国AI硬件的努力。但SemiAnalysis警告，真正全面性的限制可能促使中国开发者转向国产加速器——这正是黄仁勋一直警告的情形——破坏国际AI软件合作，并最终削弱美国高科技企业。

SemiAnalysis认为，中国继续获得美国AI加速器对美国科技产业有多重好处。第一，为AMD、英伟达和云服务提供商带来收入。第二，当中国公司从中国境外数据中心租用GPU算力时，美国当局保留监控其活动的能力，并可在出于国家安全需要时终止访问。第三，长期依赖美国硬件会降低中国开发者采用国产AI加速器的动力，否则这些国产加速器最终可能在国际市场与AMD和英伟达竞争。另一个重要方面是中国开发者对全球软件生态的贡献。中国实验室开发了DeepEP、DeepGEMM和MSA等开源技术，可提高英伟达硬件上AI工作负载的效率，惠及全球开发者；美国公司也依赖中国工程师、零部件供应商和制造商。因此，完全限制中国开发者获取美国AI加速器的法律措施，可能破坏国际合作、减少开源优化供给，并促使中国企业专为国产硬件开发软件。

另一方面，获得AMD或英伟达先进AI加速器，会使中国实验室开发出越来越复杂的AI模型，这些模型将与美国前沿模型竞争，并可能带来国家安全风险。SemiAnalysis承认，有必要限制中国获取美国公司的先进AI加速器，因为这些硬件可能被用于开发大规模杀伤性武器或以不同方式损害美国国家安全。但分析人士主张，限制应聚焦于中国实体可获得的硬件数量和能力，而不是完全禁止任何访问。SemiAnalysis似乎倾向于一种体系：中国开发者可以在美国监督下，从中国境外可信提供商租用算力。这种方式既可保留美国的技术影响力和商业利益，又可限制中国独立获取先进AI基础设施的能力。

items.title: How Shanghai fund manager Kang Wei introduced his wife Alice Huang to Jensen and built $7.5 billion Nvidia AI GPU smuggling operation
items.description: While Alice Huang lives on the headlines, it was actually her husband who put her in the same room as Jensen Huang.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Jensen Huang had a stunning fall from grace — from being one of the richest people on Earth and one of the primary drivers of the AI boom to being implicated in two extramarital affair scandals and resigning from Nvidia in under two weeks. While many are focused on the former Nvidia chief’s relationship with Alice Huang, who was allegedly passing on information to Chinese intelligence, the Wall Street Journal dug deeper into the person who introduced her to Jensen — Kang Wei, a star fund manager in Shanghai who also happened to be Ms. Huang’s husband.There have been reports that Kang Wei met Jensen Huang in the 2010s, when his investment firm was heavily involved in Chinese gaming companies. It’s not clear if this introduction predated Kang’s relationship and marriage to Alice, but sources close to Ms. Huang said that she was able to get close to Jensen by the 2020s. Despite being a couple, the WSJ reported that Kang seemingly accepted Alice’s relationship with Jensen, with people close to the couple saying that he would often joke that she was a personal assistant to the billionaire.Kang Wei is not just an average business executive, though. He made a name for himself in the finance world as a strategist for Shenyin Wanguo before taking over the Zhonghai Fund in 2007. This made him one of the youngest mutual fund chiefs in China at that time, before finally setting out on his own and founding Shanghai Hexi in 2010.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: It was also around this time that Alice Huang, whose Chinese name is Huang Le, entered the financial industry, first working at HSBC’s private banking arm in Hong Kong, before moving to CITIC Securities, where she attained a vice president position. It was during her time at CITIC that Alice crossed paths with Kang. Shanghai Hexi signed a deal with the securities firm in 2014 and 2015, and by 2016, corporate registry records show that Ms. Huang had joined the investment firm.The Economic Times reports Alice Huang’s move into Shanghai Hexi resulted in her getting a 25% stake in the company, all of which came from Kang. The remaining shares were shared between Kang Wei, with 48.75%, and his business partner, Zhu Xiaoming, with 26.25%, with Alice Huang’s 25% ownership stake being held through Shanghai Yuxi Investment Management Consulting Co., Ltd. Meanwhile, Kang also started introducing Alice Huang as his wife to his business associates and investors. You may like Alice Huang reportedly instrumental in securing over $7.5 billion of Nvidia AI GPU imports during three-year relationship with Jensen Huang Suspected Chinese spy at center of Jensen Huang affair surfaces in Beijing US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had affair with Chinese spy in honeypot operation One year later, Zhu and Kang had a falling out when one of their investments under a Hexi fund resulted in a major windfall, with the two partners disagreeing on how the profits were to be shared. Nevertheless, the massive profit generated by the deal allowed Shanghai Hexi to purchase Hangzhou Shengfeng, a video game company, for around 500 million yuan from Chinese conglomerate Century Huatong.Two years after the transaction, in 2019, Hangzhou Shengfeng’s ownership was transferred to an offshore entity, which was eventually consolidated under Osmanthus Vale Holdings — a holding company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands and listed Huang Le, Alice Huang’s Chinese name, as its sole owner. It was then purchased by 7Road Holdings less than two months after it was founded. While Ms. Huang was the signatory in this deal, it’s believed that she served as a “white glove,” a person who operates on behalf of another to conceal their identity — but it remains unclear if this was for Shanghai Hexi and Kang Wei or some other third party.There is not much information on Alice Huang’s activities between 2019 and 2021. However, Shanghai Hexi invested in Shanghai Longjing Information Technology, a data center-focused subsidiary of Century Huatong in 2020, where Ms. Huang served as a director between 2021 and 2022, according to a report by The Wire China. At about the same time, 7Road Holdings expanded into cloud computing, just before ChatGPT brought AI LLMs to the forefront. The U.S. government’s ban on the export of Nvidia chips to China put this investment in jeopardy, though, forcing it to spin off the business as 7Road International in Singapore.We don’t know when 7Road Holdings sold its Singapore subsidiary, but corporate records show that by the time the company was renamed Megaspeed in March 2023, it was already under the ownership of Huang Le Limited and led by Ms. Huang. It was sold again in November 2023 to Swiftdata, a company owned by Singaporean Tan Yong Pong. Axios said that she left the firm as a managing director soon after this acquisition, but sources said that she kept working with the company afterward, with Kang Wei helping her get it off the ground.In the same year, Shanghai Century Litong was founded to build AI data centers in Shanghai and Shenzhen, with Jiangsu Lettall Electronic Co., an electronic components manufacturer, holding a 90% stake, while the remaining 10% is owned by Century Longteng, as reported by BigGo Finance. It should be noted that Century Longteng was renamed from Shanghai Yuxi Investment Management, with the firm pivoting its business from finance to cloud computing, and that even though Alice Huang has already exited the company by this time, it’s under the control of Huang Yu, who some sources say is Ms. Huang’s sister. What to read next Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims Mass smuggling of up to 1.5 million Nvidia AI GPUs could be the underlying cause of Jensen Huang's departure, analysts claim Nvidia's Jensen Huang officially called to Congress due to reports of a Chinese spy plot A year after these data center acquisitions, Alice Huang began to be spotted in public with the former Nvidia CEO. A LinkedIn post showed her having drinks with a leather-clad Jensen Huang alongside other tech executives from NetThunder and Gigabyte at a post-Computex 2024 event. She was once again seen having dinner with him in a Taipei restaurant as reporters tried to interview him while one kid demanded his attention off camera.But more than these public sightings, Alice herself boasted about her “closeness” to the then CEO. People close to her said that she regularly posted photos with Jensen on her WeChat account, and even shared others with potential customers to help establish her credibility. She even reportedly claimed that Mr. Huang would celebrate her birthdays with restaurant dinners and gifts, with one Nvidia China sales employee also saying that she was a familiar face at the company’s annual event for China partners.An investigation revealed that from 2023 to 2025, Megaspeed imported $4.6 billion worth of Nvidia AI chips, while another $2 billion was routed through Speedmatrix, Megaspeed’s subsidiary with offices in Johor, Malaysia. Shanghai Century Litong also reportedly bought AI GPUs from other sources, with estimates putting the total number of banned chips moved through Alice Huang’s assistance at around 240,000, putting the shipments’ worth at around $7.5 billion.But even as Ms. Huang was making her international moves, Kang Wei was facing trouble at home. Chinese regulators fined him 2.5 million yuan, or approximately $380,000, in 2025, for violating sections of China’s Securities Law. This also led to a warning letter against him, issued in August 2026 by the China Securities Regulatory Commission. Despite running into trouble with the authorities, this massive paper trail showed how Kang Wei actively made moves that put Alice Huang close to Jensen Huang.Some questions remain, though, about the U.S. intelligence community’s claims that she worked with the Ministry of State Security (MSS), China’s primary intelligence and counterintelligence agency. If it’s true that Alice Huang worked with the MSS and passed on information to the agency, did she specifically target Jensen Huang, or did the spy agency simply discover their indiscretion and use that to force her to cooperate? Was all this planned by the MSS, or were they just shrewd business moves that allowed Kang to make more money while going under the radar of regulators? These are questions that only Kang Wei and Alice Huang (or the Chinese spy agency) can answer. But no matter the case, the fact remains that China acquired advanced AI chips that were supposed to be out of its reach because of this couple’s connections. items.titleZh: 上海基金经理康伟如何将妻子黄爱丽丝介绍给黄仁勋，并建立起价值75亿美元的英伟达AI GPU走私行动
items.descriptionZh:
这篇报道围绕英伟达CEO黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）的“戏剧性跌落”展开：文章称，他从全球最富有的人之一、AI热潮的主要推动者，在不到两周内因卷入两起婚外情丑闻并辞去英伟达职务。报道的重点并不在GPU技术本身，而在黄仁勋与一名据称与中国情报机构有关的女子Alice Huang（中文名黄乐）的关系，以及这条关系如何牵出规模庞大的英伟达AI芯片流向中国的网络。

《华尔街日报》进一步追查了将Alice Huang介绍给黄仁勋的人——上海明星基金经理康伟（Kang Wei），他同时也是Alice Huang的丈夫。报道称，康伟在2010年代与黄仁勋相识，当时其投资公司深度参与中国游戏公司。消息人士称，Alice Huang在2020年代得以接近黄仁勋；尽管她与康伟是夫妻，康伟似乎接受她与黄仁勋的关系，还常开玩笑称她是这位亿万富翁的“私人助理”。

文章梳理了Alice Huang的金融职业轨迹：她先在香港汇丰私人银行部门工作，后进入中信证券并升至副总裁，在此期间与康伟相识。康伟曾担任申银万国策略师，2007年接管中海基金，成为当时中国最年轻的公募基金负责人之一，2010年创立上海合熙。2014至2015年，上海合熙与中信证券签约；2016年公司登记记录显示黄乐加入该投资公司，并获得25%股份，这部分股份来自康伟；康伟持股48.75%，合伙人朱晓明持股26.25%，黄乐的25%通过上海宇熙投资管理咨询有限公司持有。康伟也开始向商业伙伴和投资者介绍黄乐为妻子。

报道称，一年后康伟与朱晓明因一笔投资基金项目巨额利润分配产生分歧，但该交易带来的利润使上海合熙得以从世纪华通手中以约5亿元人民币收购视频游戏公司杭州盛丰。2019年，杭州盛丰所有权被转移至离岸实体，最终归入在英属维尔京群岛注册的Osmanthus Vale Holdings，黄乐为唯一所有人；该公司成立不到两个月即被7Road Holdings收购。黄乐是交易签字人，报道认为她可能充当“白手套”，即为他人代持和隐匿身份，但是否代表上海合熙/康伟还是第三方仍不清楚。

2019至2021年间黄乐的活动信息不多，但2020年上海合熙投资世纪华通旗下数据中心子公司上海龙景信息技术，黄乐于2021至2022年任董事。与此同时，7Road Holdings扩展云计算业务，恰在ChatGPT推动大语言模型走向台前之前。美国禁止英伟达芯片对华出口使该业务受挫，迫使其将业务分拆为新加坡的7Road International。公司记录显示，2023年3月该公司更名为Megaspeed时，已由Huang Le Limited持有并由黄乐领导；2023年11月又出售给新加坡人Tan Yong Pong拥有的Swiftdata。Axios称黄乐在收购后不久卸任董事总经理，但消息人士称她此后继续与公司合作，康伟帮助其启动业务。

同年，上海世纪利通成立，计划在上海和深圳建设AI数据中心；江苏利通电子持股90%，世纪龙腾持股10%。世纪龙腾由上海宇熙投资管理改名而来，业务从金融转向云计算；此时黄乐已退出，公司由黄宇控制，部分消息称黄宇是黄乐的姐妹。报道还称，2024年起Alice Huang开始公开与黄仁勋同框：LinkedIn帖子显示她在Computex 2024后活动上与穿皮衣的黄仁勋及NetThunder、技嘉高管饮酒；她也被看到与黄仁勋在台北餐厅晚餐。她向身边人吹嘘与黄仁勋“关系密切”，定期在微信发布与黄的合照，甚至向潜在客户展示以建立可信度，并称黄仁勋会以餐厅晚餐和礼物为她庆生；一名英伟达中国销售员工称她是公司中国合作伙伴年度活动的熟面孔。

调查数据是报道的核心：2023至2025年，Megaspeed进口了价值46亿美元的英伟达AI芯片，另有20亿美元通过其马来西亚柔佛子公司Speedmatrix转运；上海世纪利通也从其他渠道购买AI GPU。报道估计，经Alice Huang协助转移的受限芯片约24万颗，价值约75亿美元。与此同时，康伟在中国面临监管麻烦：2025年因违反《证券法》被罚款250万元人民币（约38万美元），2026年8月中国证监会又对其发出警告函。报道认为，这一系列公司、股权和交易记录显示康伟如何主动布局，使Alice Huang得以接近黄仁勋。

文章最后提出疑问：美国情报界称Alice Huang与中国国家安全部（MSS）合作，如果属实，她是专门针对黄仁勋，还是MSS发现其私情后以此胁迫她合作？这一切是MSS策划，还是康伟为获利并规避监管而进行的精明商业运作？报道称只有康伟、Alice Huang或中国情报机构能回答。但无论哪种情况，文章认为，由于这对夫妇的人脉和运作，中国获得了本应受出口管制限制的先进AI芯片。报道所涉及的技术背景是：高性能英伟达AI GPU是训练大语言模型和建设AI数据中心的关键硬件，美国对华出口禁令使其成为稀缺战略物资，于是出现通过离岸控股、代持、第三国转口和空壳公司规避管制的路径；文章中的金额、芯片数量和股权结构，正是这种规避网络的量化体现。

items.title: macOS on PC becomes possible again thanks to Apple Silicon translator for x86-64
items.description: macOS on PCs becomes possible thanks to Apple Silicon translator for x86-64 — Hackintoshes
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The eternal spiral of computing gets yet another loop. Apple introduced its own Arm-based chips in 2020, surprising the world with a series of SoCs with a particularly high power-to-watt ratio, a perfect fit for the company's quality portables. As the designs improved on raw performance, Apple shifted away from Intel-based Macs. That meant that enterprising hackers who ran macOS on their PCs could no longer do so — until today, thanks to the Stela Apple Silicon translation layer.Stela is a minty-fresh new project from Tyler Smith, and it's just gotten started, with three releases since the first 0.1 version in barely half a day. The author warns that "it is slow and not very stable," but those warnings are somehow invisible to techies trying out a new toy. For practical purposes, Stela is a Linux-based UEFI application for loading macOS 27, presenting a virtual M2 Mac Mini to the operating system.The developer answered a couple of questions in the project's Discord server, and he remarked that the macOS image to be used is not modified at all: "Stela provides the translation and hardware behavior underneath that lets macOS go through the exact same restore process you might do on a real Mac."Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The server has seen a substantial influx of users, many of them posting photos of their PCs near-booting macOS. Predictably, most of the questions were about supporting their own particular hardware, but the excitement is palpable.To get started, all you need is to download Stela from the release pages, provide a USB stick to then boot your PC with, and, naturally, your own copy of macOS. Stela will take care of translating AArch instructions into x86-64. The translation layer uses a combination of ahead-of-time and just-in-time (JIT) compilation for the CPU, and translates Apple's Metal graphics layer calls to Mesa's NIR instructions. You may like AnyPS5 project reaches critical GPU milestone in race to enable running PS5 games natively on PC Old MacBook uses a mirror, webcam, and AI agent to code its own AMD GPU drivers Apple launches new M6 and M5 Ultra Apple silicon chips — debuting in new Mac Mini and Mac Studio The hardware requirements are basically potato-level, requiring only an x86-64-v2 — a 2008 Intel Core chip, or a 2011-vintage AMD FX processor. The author mentions that AVX2 and AVX-512 "are used when present," but woe betide you if your processor is that old to begin with. You'll need 8 GB of RAM, UEFI support, a GPT partition or entire drive, and an Nvidia card from the 16xx series to present-day 5000 models.There's no Wi-Fi support yet, and Bluetooth is limited, but the list of working Ethernet controllers is extensive, covering models from Intel, Realtek, Broadcom, Aquantia, Atheros, and even USB Ethernet sticks. The author says that he intends for Stela to eventually support all the hardware the Linux kernel does.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsPurely hypothetically, with AI automation, it's not completely insane to think that much of macOS could be pre-translated to x86-64. Yet such an endeavor has many caveats, namely the fact that a lot of code, like a browser's JIT JavaScript compilation, doesn't exist on the disk image to begin with.There's also the fact that no matter how efficient a translation layer is, the OS still needs to cryptographically accept it and run it, perhaps requiring further modification still. But we can, in fact, dream of ditching Windows for macOS without being tied to Apple's pricey and barely-repairable hardware. items.titleZh: 得益于面向 x86-64 的 Apple Silicon 转译器，在 PC 上运行 macOS 再次成为可能
items.descriptionZh:
苹果2020年转向自研Arm架构芯片后，凭借高能效比的SoC逐步取代Intel Mac，也让在普通PC上运行macOS的“黑苹果”路径基本失效。如今，开发者Tyler Smith推出新项目Stela，试图用翻译层让x86-64 PC重新运行macOS。Stela是一个基于Linux的UEFI应用，可加载macOS 27，并向操作系统呈现一台虚拟的M2 Mac Mini，使macOS认为自己运行在真实Apple Silicon硬件上。项目仍处早期：首个0.1版本发布后半天内已连发三个版本，作者警告其“速度慢且不太稳定”，但技术社区反应热烈，Discord服务器涌入大量用户，许多人晒出PC接近启动macOS的照片，问题多集中在具体硬件支持上。

核心技术方面，Stela负责把AArch指令翻译为x86-64指令，采用提前编译（AOT）与即时编译（JIT）相结合的方式处理CPU代码；同时将苹果Metal图形层调用翻译为Mesa的NIR中间表示，以便在x86 PC的图形栈上执行。开发者强调，所使用的macOS镜像并未被修改：Stela在底层提供翻译和硬件行为模拟，让macOS可以走与真实Mac相同的恢复流程。使用方式是从发布页下载Stela，准备USB盘启动PC，并自备macOS副本。

硬件门槛相对较低，但限制明显。CPU仅需x86-64-v2，相当于2008年的Intel Core或2011年的AMD FX处理器；若处理器支持AVX2和AVX-512则会启用。内存要求8GB，需要UEFI支持和GPT分区或整块硬盘，显卡目前要求Nvidia 16xx系列至5000系列。网络方面尚不支持Wi-Fi，蓝牙支持有限，但以太网控制器兼容列表较广，涵盖Intel、Realtek、Broadcom、Aquantia、Atheros以及USB以太网适配器。开发者表示，未来目标是支持Linux内核所能支持的全部硬件。

从影响看，Stela为在非苹果硬件上运行macOS提供了新思路，可能延长旧PC寿命、降低体验macOS的门槛，并推动操作系统翻译与图形兼容研究。但短期内它更适合爱好者和实验场景，不适合日常使用。文章也指出，理论上可通过AI自动化把大量macOS代码预翻译为x86-64，但存在明显限制：浏览器JIT JavaScript等大量代码并不存在于磁盘镜像中；而且无论翻译层多高效，操作系统仍需在加密层面接受并运行相关代码，可能还需要进一步修改。尽管如此，Stela让“摆脱Windows、又不必绑定苹果昂贵且难维修硬件”的设想重新变得值得期待。

history.title: Malaysia and Singapore step up Nvidia AI chip probes amidst Jensen Huang controversy
history.description: Malaysia is investigating possible re-exports of Nvidia AI hardware amid concerns about circumvention of U.S. restrictions on China as Singapore charges an executive over suspicious purchases of 917 AI servers.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Malaysia and Singapore have intensified scrutiny of AI hardware shipments amid concerns about the potential circumvention of U.S. export restrictions on China. Malaysia has launched an investigation into whether AI hardware imported by a subsidiary of the ill-fated Megaspeed was subsequently exported to other countries, reports Reuters. Meanwhile, Singapore has charged another executive over questionable purchases of 917 servers that may contain Nvidia accelerators, according to The Straits Times. The news follows the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over claims he had multiple extra-marital affairs, including with a possible Chinese intelligence asset who facilitated GPU smuggling into China. Analysts speculate that systematic chip smuggling may be the reason behind his departure.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedMalaysia's Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry is examining whether Speedmatrix, the Malaysian subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed, re-exported any of the AI processors and servers it had imported for use in local data centers. Apparently, after months of investigating, authorities have yet to find out whether any such shipments occurred and, if they did, whether they complied with Malaysian laws. Malaysia introduced restrictions on the export, transit, and trans-shipment of advanced U.S.-developed AI accelerators in July 2025, so it now requires companies to obtain appropriate permits.The Malaysian ministry said it was cooperating with customs authorities as well as officials in Singapore and the U.S., and could introduce additional restrictions. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said there was no evidence that Megaspeed-related AI hardware had left Malaysia, but he promised to cooperate with international investigations.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Speaking of Megaspeed, the company said on November 12 that it had hired a U.S. law firm to conduct a comprehensive inventory of its AI GPUs and independently assess its compliance with U.S. export-control regulations, reports DigiTimes. The company also confirmed that it had cooperated with inspections by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) and was prepared to cooperate with other U.S. government agencies if necessary.James Tan Yong Pong, chief executive of Megaspeed, stressed that compliance with U.S. export rules as well as transparent operations were always a priority for the company. However, Megaspeed did not disclose how many GPUs it owns and which GPU models it has, what BIS examined during its inspections, or whether the authorities had identified any violations. You may like Nvidia tightens tracking of AI GPUs in Southeast Asia as Chinese chip smuggling draws scrutiny, report claims Mass smuggling of up to 1.5 million Nvidia AI GPUs could be the underlying cause of Jensen Huang's departure, analysts claim Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims Meanwhile, Singaporean authorities have brought 41 criminal charges against Shi Bingzhe, a 34-year-old Chinese citizen who served as director of Superphi and chief operating officer of NJ Global Financial. The two companies purchased 917 servers containing restricted Nvidia hardware from Aperia International in 41 transactions between May 2024 and February 2025, according to prosecutors. Authorities allege that the companies had reason to believe the servers were linked to criminal activity by Aperia International. Superphi now faces six charges, while NJ Global Financial faces 35.The latest charges expand a case that now involves five individuals and six companies. Four firms — Aperia International, A-Speed Infotech, Aperia Cloud Services (II), and Luxuriate Your Life — were charged in July over allegedly making false claims when purchasing servers. Meanwhile, the exact nature of those claims was not disclosed in the report. Authorities have frozen the disposal of a property worth approximately S$55 million and confiscated around S$1 million from bank accounts. Shi faces up to 10 years in prison and a fine of S$500,000 per charge if convicted. His next court appearance is scheduled for January 4, 2027.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe two cases largely highlight the significance of Malaysia and Singapore in the supply chain of restricted AI hardware to places where it should not be, such as China. Singapore's investigation focuses on alleged fraud and transactions involving proceeds of criminal activity, whereas Malaysia seeks to find out whether imported AI equipment was subsequently shipped abroad in violation of local regulations.Neither investigation has found that the hardware ultimately reached China, but both illustrate difficulties that authorities face as they attempt to enforce restrictions on advanced AI hardware across international supply chains. history.titleZh: 马来西亚和新加坡在黄仁勋争议中加强对英伟达AI芯片的调查
history.descriptionZh:
这篇报道聚焦美国对华先进AI芯片出口限制背景下，马来西亚和新加坡对AI硬件转运与走私风险的执法升级。文章称，马来西亚正在调查已陷入风波的Megaspeed旗下马来西亚子公司Speedmatrix，是否将原本进口用于本地数据中心的AI处理器和服务器再出口至其他国家；新加坡则就917台可能含有Nvidia加速器的服务器采购问题，对另一名高管提出刑事指控。原文还将这些调查与所谓Nvidia CEO黄仁勋因婚外情及可能涉及中国情报资产而辞职的传闻联系起来，并称分析师猜测系统性芯片走私可能是其离职原因。需要指出，这部分说法缺乏公开证据支持，摘要仅反映原文叙述。

背景上，美国限制先进AI加速器对华出口，东南亚被视为可能的转口和转运节点。马来西亚投资、贸易和工业部正在核查Speedmatrix是否违反当地规定。马来西亚于2025年7月对美国开发的高级AI加速器的出口、过境和转运实施限制，要求相关企业取得许可。马方表示正与海关、新加坡和美国官员合作，并可能出台更多限制。马来西亚总理安瓦尔·易卜拉欣称，没有证据显示与Megaspeed相关的AI硬件已离开马来西亚，但承诺配合国际调查。

Megaspeed于11月12日称已聘请美国律所对其AI GPU进行全面盘点，并独立评估其是否符合美国出口管制规定；公司还确认配合美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）检查，并准备在必要时配合其他美国政府机构。CEO James Tan Yong Pong强调，遵守美国出口规则和透明运营始终是公司优先事项。但Megaspeed未披露其GPU数量、型号、BIS检查具体内容，也未说明当局是否发现违规。

新加坡方面，34岁中国公民Shi Bingzhe被控41项刑事罪名。他曾任Superphi董事和NJ Global Financial首席运营官。检方称，两家公司在2024年5月至2025年2月间通过41笔交易，从Aperia International购买917台含受限Nvidia硬件的服务器，并有理由相信这些服务器与Aperia International的犯罪活动有关。Superphi面临6项指控，NJ Global Financial面临35项。案件已涉及5名个人和6家公司；Aperia International、A-Speed Infotech、Aperia Cloud Services (II)和Luxuriate Your Life四家公司此前因购买服务器时涉嫌虚假陈述于7月被控，但报道未披露虚假陈述的具体性质。当局冻结了价值约5500万新元财产的处置，并从银行账户没收约100万新元。若罪名成立，Shi每项罪名最高可判10年监禁及50万新元罚款，下次出庭定于2027年1月4日。

从技术原理看，此类案件的核心不是新产品创新，而是先进AI加速器出口管制与供应链合规。受限GPU通常用于数据中心的大规模AI训练和推理，具有高算力、高带宽和高价值特征，是美国对华技术限制的重点。规避路径可能包括第三国转口、过境转运、虚假最终用户声明、整机与部件混装、以及利用区域数据中心作为名义最终用途等。马来西亚的新许可制度正是针对出口、过境和转运环节补上监管缺口；新加坡案件则侧重欺诈、虚假陈述和犯罪所得交易。

原文未提供具体GPU型号、算力、带宽、功耗等性能参数，也没有不同芯片之间的性能对比数据。可量化的信息主要是：917台服务器、41笔交易、41项指控、5名个人和6家公司、约5500万新元冻结财产、约100万新元没收金额、每项罪名最高10年监禁和50万新元罚款，以及马来西亚2025年7月的管制措施和Megaspeed 11月12日的合规声明。

影响和应用场景方面，两起案件说明新加坡和马来西亚在受限AI硬件供应链中的关键节点地位，也显示各国执法机构在跨国供应链中追踪最终流向的难度。对数据中心运营商、服务器集成商和云服务商而言，需要加强最终用户审查、转售和再出口合规、GPU资产盘点与可追溯性。两起调查均尚未认定相关硬件最终进入中国，但已凸显美国出口限制在东南亚执行中的复杂性和合规风险。

history.title: ‘Broken and shattered’ Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang surrendered during resignation meeting, report claims
history.description: Jensen Huang reportedly called himself 'a piece of sh--" after his forced departure, but employees still want him back.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 39 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly called himself “a piece of sh**" as he left the company he built over 33 years. Bloomberg reports that the co-founder, known for his legendary energy and outgoing demeanor, surrendered and looked “broken and shattered” during the board meeting where he resigned from the AI hardware firm after admitting to at least one extra-marital affair, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. But despite his resignation and the controversies surrounding him, it seems that Nvidia employees are still rallying behind him, with thousands of comments on the company’s internal “suggestion box” showing support for the disgraced leader, according to Wired.“If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” one commenter said, while another one wrote, “We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance.” An Nvidia staffer told Wired privately, “Nvidia is Nvidia because of Jensen,” even as another employee sent a company-wide email demanding transparency into his resignation. “I stand by Jensen. Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us.” They also added, “If America fails the man who helped build its future, then this world does not deserve Jensen Huang.”According to the report, internal calls for Huang's reinstatement have drawn more than 1,600 comments on Nvidia's internal forums, "the majority in full support of reinstalling him." The company has more than 42,000 employees worldwide.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Rumors about Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, being close to Jensen Huang first circulated in late October, with Nvidia vehemently denying there was any impropriety. “Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” an Nvidia spokesperson told Tom's Hardware. However, things took a turn for the worse for the Nvidia CEO when reports came out that he actually had an affair with Ms. Huang.Nvidia General Counsel and Secretary of the Board Tim Teter confronted Jensen at his house when this came out, after which he confessed. The founder soon released a statement admitting to and apologizing for his actions, while the company’s board formed an independent committee to investigate. However, another scandal broke out revealing that the former Nvidia chief had another affair — this time with a subordinate. This was apparently the last straw for the board, and the Nvidia co-founder was forced to resign soon after. But, more importantly, he was the face of the company who was particularly loved by many people, giving rise to the term “Jensanity” in his home country of Taiwan. Regardless of his status as a billionaire, people still find him trying out street food, eating at fast food chains, and even honoring his humble beginnings as a busboy at Denny’s.Aside from these latest scandals, many gamers castigate Huang for abandoning the core market that supported Nvidia before it became an AI giant, with consumer graphics cards now drastically more expensive than ever before. history.title: Mass smuggling of up to 1.5 million Nvidia AI GPUs could be the underlying cause of Jensen Huang's departure, analysts claim
history.description: Top analyst firm SemiAnalysis says it has tracked staggering 1.5 gigawatts of banned AI accelerators flowing into China.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 11 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Leading semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis believes that Jensen Huang's sudden departure from Nvidia may have been driven not only by revelations about his personal extramarital relationships, but also by widespread illicit exports of advanced AI accelerators to China. In its latest newsletter, analysts estimate that more than 1.5 gigawatts (GW) worth of restricted Nvidia hardware, which could be equivalent to up to 1.5 million GPUs, has reached the country despite U.S. export controls.Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc)While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply marketThe state of China's decade-long semiconductor pushHuawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fabChina's latest round of rare-earth export controls explainedOver 1.5 GW of Nvidia hardware subject to U.S. export restrictions ultimately ended up in China in recent years, according to SemiAnalysis' Accelerator Model, which tracks AI accelerator production and destinations. The estimate excludes processors that Nvidia specifically developed to comply with U.S. export rules, such as the H20 or H800. The firm also claims that the U.S. Department of Commerce has reached a similar conclusion about the scale of unauthorized shipments. Yet, SemiAnalysis does not disclose the exact number of accelerators shipped to China illegally, or their split between Nvidia's product generations.The scale of the alleged diversions is particularly notable because modern AI accelerators require substantial power and infrastructure. While the report does not explain how it converts accelerator quantities into power figures, it is likely that the company uses package-level nameplate/rated power multiplied by the number of GPUs. Assuming that all of these AI GPUs were Nvidia H200 SXM rated for up to 700W, then China got around 2.142 million of such accelerators, while if all of these processors were B200 SXM rated for up to 1,000W, then we are talking about 1.5 million units. For a mixed deployment, the total would fall between these figures, depending on the proportion of H200 and B200 accelerators. To put these numbers into context, xAI's Colossus One had 220-230,000 Hopper H100 and H200 GPUs, whereas the Colossus 2 has a target of 1.2 million Blackwell B200 and B300 GPUs. That said, 1.5 GW of restricted Nvidia hardware in China represents an enormous amount of computing infrastructure, which is comparable, or even exceeds, the scale of xAI's entire existing Colossus operation.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While SemiAnalysis did not reveal all the cases in which restricted AI accelerators reached the People's Republic of China, it supports its assessment with two well-known cases of alleged GPU smuggling. The first involves Supermicro co-founder Wally Liaw, Taiwan sales executive Steven Chang, and contractor Willy Sun, who were charged in March 2026. According to the indictment, approximately $2.5 billion worth of servers were sold to a company in Southeast Asia, with $510 million worth of equipment subsequently diverted to China and obtained by Alibaba. Prosecutors allege that the defendants used substitute servers and transferred identification labels to conceal the actual destinations of the hardware during audits.The second case involves nine individuals associated with Nvidia, Albatron, Chief Telecom, Flying Tiger, and Supermicro in Taiwan. The authorities accuse the group of arranging unauthorized exports of 130 Nvidia B300-based servers, 74 of which eventually reached China. The suspects used shell companies, forged documents, and declared Japan as the destination for servers that were actually bound for China, according to prosecutors. Taiwanese authorities discovered the operation during a drug smuggling investigation. Both cases are still before the courts. You may like How Shanghai fund manager Kang Wei introduced his wife Alice Huang to Jensen and built $7.5 billion Nvidia AI GPU smuggling operation Investigative report details how export-restricted Nvidia AI chips reach China Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims Amidst the ongoing fallout and reports into Jensen's Huang's extramarital affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence asset who was an executive at Megaspeed, one report claims that Ms. Huang was personally responsible for facilitating the smuggling of $7.5 billion of Nvidia AI hardware into China, around 240,000 GPUs, mostly H100 and H200 models.The right timing?SemiAnalysis suggests that the scale of these violations may explain why Huang's personal conduct became a major issue at this very point in time. The company's analysts speculate that some members of the U.S. intelligence community sought to remove Jensen Huang because he opposed more aggressive restrictions on China's access to American AI hardware. However, the report provides no direct evidence that intelligence agencies influenced Nvidia's board or that Huang participated in unauthorized exports.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe timing also coincides with congressional efforts to advance the Remote Access Security Act (RASA), which passed the House of Representatives on January 12. The legislation is meant to extend U.S. export-control authority to remote access to advanced AI hardware hosted outside China, including data centers in Europe and the Middle East. SemiAnalysis reports that Nvidia and Oracle have actively opposed the proposal.The analysts believe that Huang's departure essentially removes an influential opponent of stricter restrictions and accelerates efforts to block Chinese companies from accessing American AI hardware in the cloud. However, SemiAnalysis warns that truly all-inclusive restrictions could encourage Chinese developers to adopt domestic accelerators (something that Jensen Huang has consistently warned about), undermine international AI software collaboration, and ultimately weaken American high-tech companies.Continued Chinese access to American AI accelerators offers several advantages to the U.S. technology industry, according to SemiAnalysis. Firstly, it generates revenue for American companies such as AMD, Nvidia, and cloud service providers. Secondly, when Chinese companies rent GPU capacity from data centers outside China, U.S. authorities retain the ability to monitor their activities and potentially terminate access if necessary due to national security concerns. Thirdly, prolonged reliance on American hardware reduces incentives for Chinese developers to adopt domestic AI accelerators, which could eventually compete with AMD and Nvidia in international markets. What to read next Nvidia tightens tracking of AI GPUs in Southeast Asia as Chinese chip smuggling draws scrutiny, report claims Chinese AI companies buy 1 million Nvidia GPUs in a single year, report claims Alice Huang reportedly instrumental in securing over $7.5 billion of Nvidia AI GPU imports during three-year relationship with Jensen Huang Another important aspect is the contribution of Chinese developers to the global software ecosystem. On the one hand, Chinese laboratories have developed open-source technologies such as DeepEP, DeepGEMM, and MSA, which improve the efficiency of AI workloads on Nvidia hardware and benefit developers worldwide. In addition, American companies also depend on Chinese engineers, component suppliers, and manufacturers. Therefore, legal curbs that completely restrict Chinese developers' access to American AI accelerators could undermine international cooperation, reduce availability of open-source optimizations, and encourage Chinese companies to develop software specifically for domestic hardware.On the other hand, access to advanced AI accelerators from AMD or Nvidia enables Chinese laboratories to develop increasingly sophisticated AI models, which will rival leading-edge models developed in America and perhaps create national security risks. To that end, SemiAnalysis acknowledges the need to limit China's access to advanced AI accelerators from U.S.-based companies, as they could, among other things, be used to develop weapons of mass destruction or undermine American national security in different ways. Yet, SA analysts argue that restrictions should focus on the amount and capabilities of hardware available to Chinese entities rather than completely prohibit any access.SemiAnalysis seems to favor a system in which Chinese developers can rent computing capacity from trusted providers outside China under U.S. oversight. Such an approach could preserve American technological influence and commercial benefits and limit China's ability to acquire advanced AI infrastructure independently. history.titleZh: 分析师称，多达150万块英伟达AI GPU的大规模走私可能是黄仁勋离职的根本原因
history.descriptionZh:
据半导体研究机构SemiAnalysis分析，英伟达CEO黄仁勋突然离开英伟达，可能不仅与其个人婚外情曝光有关，也与大量受美国出口管制的先进AI加速器流入中国有关。SemiAnalysis在其最新通讯中估计，近年来已有超过1.5吉瓦（GW）的受限英伟达硬件进入中国，按不同GPU型号折算，相当于最多约150万块GPU。该估算来自其“Accelerator Model”，该模型追踪AI加速器的生产和最终目的地，并排除了英伟达为符合美国出口规则而专门开发的产品，如H20和H800。SemiAnalysis还称，美国商务部对未授权出货规模得出了类似结论，但未披露非法输华加速器的确切数量及代际分布。

1.5GW这一规模之所以引人关注，是因为现代AI加速器需要大量电力和基础设施。报告未说明如何将加速器数量换算为功率，但很可能是用封装级额定功率乘以GPU数量。若全部按最高700W的英伟达H200 SXM计算，中国获得约214.2万块此类加速器；若全部按最高1000W的B200 SXM计算，则约为150万块；混合部署则介于两者之间。作为对比，xAI的Colossus One拥有22万至23万块Hopper H100和H200 GPU，Colossus 2的目标是120万块Blackwell B200和B300 GPU。也就是说，1.5GW受限英伟达硬件所代表的算力基础设施规模巨大，可与xAI现有整个Colossus运营规模相当，甚至更大。

SemiAnalysis并未披露受限AI加速器进入中国的所有案例，但用两个已知的GPU走私案支撑其判断。第一案涉及Supermicro联合创始人Wally Liaw、台湾销售主管Steven Chang和承包商Willy Sun，三人于2026年3月被起诉。起诉书称，约25亿美元的服务器被卖给东南亚一家公司，其中5.1亿美元设备随后被转往中国并由阿里巴巴获得；被告据称在审计期间使用替代服务器和转移识别标签来掩盖硬件的真实目的地。第二案涉及与英伟达、Albatron、Chief Telecom、Flying Tiger和Supermicro台湾相关的九名个人。当局指控该团伙安排130台基于英伟达B300的服务器未经授权出口，其中74台最终到达中国。检方称，嫌疑人使用空壳公司、伪造文件，并将实际运往中国的服务器申报为日本目的地；台湾当局是在一项毒品走私调查中发现该操作的。两案目前仍在法院审理中。

另有报道称，在与黄仁勋保持三年关系的Alice Huang期间，她据称促成约75亿美元的英伟达AI硬件、约24万块GPU（多为H100和H200）进入中国。SemiAnalysis暗示，这些违规行为的规模可能解释为何黄仁勋的个人行为在此时成为重大问题。其分析师猜测，美国情报界部分成员可能希望移除黄仁勋，因为他反对更激进地限制中国获取美国AI硬件。但报告没有提供直接证据表明情报机构影响了英伟达董事会，或黄仁勋参与了未授权出口。

这一时间点也恰逢美国国会推进《远程访问安全法案》（RASA）。该法案于1月12日在众议院通过，旨在将美国出口管制权限扩展到对中国境外先进AI硬件的远程访问，包括欧洲和中东的数据中心。SemiAnalysis称，英伟达和甲骨文积极反对该提案。分析人士认为，黄仁勋的离开实质上移除了更严格限制的一位有影响力反对者，并可能加速阻止中国公司通过云端访问美国AI硬件的努力。但SemiAnalysis警告，真正全面性的限制可能促使中国开发者转向国产加速器——这正是黄仁勋一直警告的情形——破坏国际AI软件合作，并最终削弱美国高科技企业。

SemiAnalysis认为，中国继续获得美国AI加速器对美国科技产业有多重好处。第一，为AMD、英伟达和云服务提供商带来收入。第二，当中国公司从中国境外数据中心租用GPU算力时，美国当局保留监控其活动的能力，并可在出于国家安全需要时终止访问。第三，长期依赖美国硬件会降低中国开发者采用国产AI加速器的动力，否则这些国产加速器最终可能在国际市场与AMD和英伟达竞争。另一个重要方面是中国开发者对全球软件生态的贡献。中国实验室开发了DeepEP、DeepGEMM和MSA等开源技术，可提高英伟达硬件上AI工作负载的效率，惠及全球开发者；美国公司也依赖中国工程师、零部件供应商和制造商。因此，完全限制中国开发者获取美国AI加速器的法律措施，可能破坏国际合作、减少开源优化供给，并促使中国企业专为国产硬件开发软件。

另一方面，获得AMD或英伟达先进AI加速器，会使中国实验室开发出越来越复杂的AI模型，这些模型将与美国前沿模型竞争，并可能带来国家安全风险。SemiAnalysis承认，有必要限制中国获取美国公司的先进AI加速器，因为这些硬件可能被用于开发大规模杀伤性武器或以不同方式损害美国国家安全。但分析人士主张，限制应聚焦于中国实体可获得的硬件数量和能力，而不是完全禁止任何访问。SemiAnalysis似乎倾向于一种体系：中国开发者可以在美国监督下，从中国境外可信提供商租用算力。这种方式既可保留美国的技术影响力和商业利益，又可限制中国独立获取先进AI基础设施的能力。

history.title: How Shanghai fund manager Kang Wei introduced his wife Alice Huang to Jensen and built $7.5 billion Nvidia AI GPU smuggling operation
history.description: While Alice Huang lives on the headlines, it was actually her husband who put her in the same room as Jensen Huang.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Jensen Huang had a stunning fall from grace — from being one of the richest people on Earth and one of the primary drivers of the AI boom to being implicated in two extramarital affair scandals and resigning from Nvidia in under two weeks. While many are focused on the former Nvidia chief’s relationship with Alice Huang, who was allegedly passing on information to Chinese intelligence, the Wall Street Journal dug deeper into the person who introduced her to Jensen — Kang Wei, a star fund manager in Shanghai who also happened to be Ms. Huang’s husband.There have been reports that Kang Wei met Jensen Huang in the 2010s, when his investment firm was heavily involved in Chinese gaming companies. It’s not clear if this introduction predated Kang’s relationship and marriage to Alice, but sources close to Ms. Huang said that she was able to get close to Jensen by the 2020s. Despite being a couple, the WSJ reported that Kang seemingly accepted Alice’s relationship with Jensen, with people close to the couple saying that he would often joke that she was a personal assistant to the billionaire.Kang Wei is not just an average business executive, though. He made a name for himself in the finance world as a strategist for Shenyin Wanguo before taking over the Zhonghai Fund in 2007. This made him one of the youngest mutual fund chiefs in China at that time, before finally setting out on his own and founding Shanghai Hexi in 2010.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: It was also around this time that Alice Huang, whose Chinese name is Huang Le, entered the financial industry, first working at HSBC’s private banking arm in Hong Kong, before moving to CITIC Securities, where she attained a vice president position. It was during her time at CITIC that Alice crossed paths with Kang. Shanghai Hexi signed a deal with the securities firm in 2014 and 2015, and by 2016, corporate registry records show that Ms. Huang had joined the investment firm.The Economic Times reports Alice Huang’s move into Shanghai Hexi resulted in her getting a 25% stake in the company, all of which came from Kang. The remaining shares were shared between Kang Wei, with 48.75%, and his business partner, Zhu Xiaoming, with 26.25%, with Alice Huang’s 25% ownership stake being held through Shanghai Yuxi Investment Management Consulting Co., Ltd. Meanwhile, Kang also started introducing Alice Huang as his wife to his business associates and investors. You may like Alice Huang reportedly instrumental in securing over $7.5 billion of Nvidia AI GPU imports during three-year relationship with Jensen Huang Suspected Chinese spy at center of Jensen Huang affair surfaces in Beijing US intelligence believes Jensen Huang had affair with Chinese spy in honeypot operation One year later, Zhu and Kang had a falling out when one of their investments under a Hexi fund resulted in a major windfall, with the two partners disagreeing on how the profits were to be shared. Nevertheless, the massive profit generated by the deal allowed Shanghai Hexi to purchase Hangzhou Shengfeng, a video game company, for around 500 million yuan from Chinese conglomerate Century Huatong.Two years after the transaction, in 2019, Hangzhou Shengfeng’s ownership was transferred to an offshore entity, which was eventually consolidated under Osmanthus Vale Holdings — a holding company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands and listed Huang Le, Alice Huang’s Chinese name, as its sole owner. It was then purchased by 7Road Holdings less than two months after it was founded. While Ms. Huang was the signatory in this deal, it’s believed that she served as a “white glove,” a person who operates on behalf of another to conceal their identity — but it remains unclear if this was for Shanghai Hexi and Kang Wei or some other third party.There is not much information on Alice Huang’s activities between 2019 and 2021. However, Shanghai Hexi invested in Shanghai Longjing Information Technology, a data center-focused subsidiary of Century Huatong in 2020, where Ms. Huang served as a director between 2021 and 2022, according to a report by The Wire China. At about the same time, 7Road Holdings expanded into cloud computing, just before ChatGPT brought AI LLMs to the forefront. The U.S. government’s ban on the export of Nvidia chips to China put this investment in jeopardy, though, forcing it to spin off the business as 7Road International in Singapore.We don’t know when 7Road Holdings sold its Singapore subsidiary, but corporate records show that by the time the company was renamed Megaspeed in March 2023, it was already under the ownership of Huang Le Limited and led by Ms. Huang. It was sold again in November 2023 to Swiftdata, a company owned by Singaporean Tan Yong Pong. Axios said that she left the firm as a managing director soon after this acquisition, but sources said that she kept working with the company afterward, with Kang Wei helping her get it off the ground.In the same year, Shanghai Century Litong was founded to build AI data centers in Shanghai and Shenzhen, with Jiangsu Lettall Electronic Co., an electronic components manufacturer, holding a 90% stake, while the remaining 10% is owned by Century Longteng, as reported by BigGo Finance. It should be noted that Century Longteng was renamed from Shanghai Yuxi Investment Management, with the firm pivoting its business from finance to cloud computing, and that even though Alice Huang has already exited the company by this time, it’s under the control of Huang Yu, who some sources say is Ms. Huang’s sister. What to read next Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang may have been the target of a spy plot through 'Chinese intelligence asset,' report claims Mass smuggling of up to 1.5 million Nvidia AI GPUs could be the underlying cause of Jensen Huang's departure, analysts claim Nvidia's Jensen Huang officially called to Congress due to reports of a Chinese spy plot A year after these data center acquisitions, Alice Huang began to be spotted in public with the former Nvidia CEO. A LinkedIn post showed her having drinks with a leather-clad Jensen Huang alongside other tech executives from NetThunder and Gigabyte at a post-Computex 2024 event. She was once again seen having dinner with him in a Taipei restaurant as reporters tried to interview him while one kid demanded his attention off camera.But more than these public sightings, Alice herself boasted about her “closeness” to the then CEO. People close to her said that she regularly posted photos with Jensen on her WeChat account, and even shared others with potential customers to help establish her credibility. She even reportedly claimed that Mr. Huang would celebrate her birthdays with restaurant dinners and gifts, with one Nvidia China sales employee also saying that she was a familiar face at the company’s annual event for China partners.An investigation revealed that from 2023 to 2025, Megaspeed imported $4.6 billion worth of Nvidia AI chips, while another $2 billion was routed through Speedmatrix, Megaspeed’s subsidiary with offices in Johor, Malaysia. Shanghai Century Litong also reportedly bought AI GPUs from other sources, with estimates putting the total number of banned chips moved through Alice Huang’s assistance at around 240,000, putting the shipments’ worth at around $7.5 billion.But even as Ms. Huang was making her international moves, Kang Wei was facing trouble at home. Chinese regulators fined him 2.5 million yuan, or approximately $380,000, in 2025, for violating sections of China’s Securities Law. This also led to a warning letter against him, issued in August 2026 by the China Securities Regulatory Commission. Despite running into trouble with the authorities, this massive paper trail showed how Kang Wei actively made moves that put Alice Huang close to Jensen Huang.Some questions remain, though, about the U.S. intelligence community’s claims that she worked with the Ministry of State Security (MSS), China’s primary intelligence and counterintelligence agency. If it’s true that Alice Huang worked with the MSS and passed on information to the agency, did she specifically target Jensen Huang, or did the spy agency simply discover their indiscretion and use that to force her to cooperate? Was all this planned by the MSS, or were they just shrewd business moves that allowed Kang to make more money while going under the radar of regulators? These are questions that only Kang Wei and Alice Huang (or the Chinese spy agency) can answer. But no matter the case, the fact remains that China acquired advanced AI chips that were supposed to be out of its reach because of this couple’s connections.
